analysis.title: Telecom: Starlink's 80K Towers - Real Deal, or A Tightening Bear Hug?
key_insights: Bloomberg reported Thursday after-market that SpaceX aims to secure 80K+ US cell sites, naming Crown Castle as the tower operator. Wolfe says the rumor is easy to believe after Starlink's recent agreement to purchase low-band spectrum.

80K towers is a lot for a low-band (coverage-focused) spectrum strategy, which implies more capacity per cell than Wolfe previously estimated. Wolfe raises its estimate of Starlink's theoretical upper limit on 800MHz to about 24M US phones served.
Spectrum auctions in 2027/28 give SpaceX the chance to expand its mid-band (capacity-focused) portfolio.
Starlink lacks the spectral depth to serve a large share of mobile customers. Its financial impact on US retail mobile is at worst years away.

Speculation about a Starlink-Verizon MVNO (wholesale network access deal) followed David Faber's comments on CNBC. Wolfe calls the comments theoretical and says it is too early for a Big 3 carrier to fold because Big 3 enterprise valuation multiples are not low enough yet.
Verizon management brushed off the idea of a 'prisoner's dilemma' at September conferences, with VZ shares not far from today's level.

Wolfe thinks SpaceX's mobile ambitions may extend to, and originate from, serving a fleet of Teslas, Optimus robots and drones. If so, Musk need not be convinced of a stand-alone ROIC in retail wireless to see strategic benefit.

Wolfe expects technical bounces in telecom stocks to be sold before they get far, because industry structure is in question even though fundamentals are sturdy. Timing of scale is semantics, and the eventual structural threat from a 4th carrier is what should be priced into the sector.
Buying telecom stocks for a trade is possible, but Wolfe sees limited upside.
Ratings: Telecom sector Market Weight. CHTR Underperform ($118 PT), T Outperform ($26 PT), TMUS, VZ and CMCSA Peer Perform.

market_movers.rationale: Wolfe keeps Underperform with an $118 target, 8.6% shown in the % UP column. Rating history shows the target was cut to $118 on 09/14/26.
Wolfe keeps Outperform with a $26 target, 24.2% upside. Rating history shows the target was lowered to $26 on 10/22/26.
Peer Perform, no target assigned. Wolfe sees no near-term need for Verizon to enter an MVNO deal with Starlink.

sector_views.rationale: Market Weight. Fundamentals are sturdy, but the structural risk of a 4th carrier from Starlink limits upside and Wolfe expects technical bounces to be sold.

risk_factors: Starlink becoming a 4th US carrier is the structural threat Wolfe says should be priced into the telecom sector.
Starlink could expand mid-band capacity in the 2027/28 spectrum auctions.
A Big 3 carrier could strike an MVNO deal with Starlink, though Wolfe thinks it is too early.
Cable mobile could use rising scale to renegotiate MVNO pricing, a stated downside risk for Verizon.
Wolfe lists competition from satellite rollouts as a downside risk for Comcast.
vol_and_positioning: Wolfe expects technical bounces in telecom stocks to be sold before they get very far.
